result.coverage:
I checked all 42 first-class masterclass main lessons (the registry.ts OPENINGS list, via ALL_LESSONS scope 'main'). Variation, trap and gambit-tab lessons were not checked. For each lesson:
- I replayed every beat's moves with chess.js. No illegal moves were found.
- I took the deepest beat as the main spine and checked it against openings-lichess.json. Every spine follows a DB line for at least 7 plies (Bird's and Réti only as a prefix of a longer DB entry).
- I recorded the terminal FEN, castling rights and minor pieces still at home, as a Gate B proxy.
- I ran Stockfish on every terminal from the student's side (depth 16; the flagged ones again at depth 18).
- I scanned each `say` for '<piece> on <sq>' and '<sq>-<piece>' claims against the board at that beat. The 15 hits were hand-checked; most are historical or hypothetical references and were dismissed.

What I could not check:
- The masters spine past the Lichess DB anchor. The tails were not compared with the masters explorer because that needs the network proxy.
- Narration claims phrased in other ways (pins, attacks, 'controls', material counts) were read only for the beats listed above, not across all beats.

Orphans: every lesson file in src/data/lessons is imported somewhere, so there is no dead lesson code in scope. This was a read-only audit, so nothing was removed.

Scratch scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-chess-academy-pro/61fdf752-44c7-57cb-be1e-44a85a8d5754/scratchpad (a.ts, b.ts, c.ts, ev.mjs, out.json, fens.tsv).

result.coverage: Checked all 328 variation lessons from ALL_LESSONS in registry.ts: the 315 on the 42 masterclass openings plus 13 gambit-tab lessons. I also measured the shared prefix with each opening's main lesson, did pairwise distinctness checks inside each opening (prefix, same final FEN, at least 80% overlap), confirmed sources are present and well-formed (all 328 have sources), confirmed orientation matches repertoire.json, and counted move-number prefixes. Not done: hand-reading the remaining prose sentences for board truth, Stockfish soundness of each terminus (not run), checking that source URLs resolve, and checking sayShort word counts (my word counter disagreed with the gate's tokenisation, so I dropped that check). findings.evidence: Final FEN rn1q1rk1/pp2bppp/1n1pp3/7b/2PP4/2N2N1P/PP2BPP1/R1BQ1RK1. findings.evidence: Continuity test compares only the pawn set, against every ply of every line including ply 0, ignoring pieces, castling and which tab shows the plan; allEntries loads repertoire+pro+anti but not gambits.json (4 gambit plans unchecked) and skips -endgame plans: all 48 provably unreachable plans pass. Theme test builds colorMap with Array.isArray(proRaw) but pro-repertoires.json is {players, openings}, so the 317 pro plans (and the 23 anti / 8 gambit plans, never loaded) count opponent moves as student moves; COND drops any break containing 'passed', and themeEmpty requires goals.size > 0, so mp-procarlsen-ruy-endgame (only break 'c4-c5 passed-pawn push') passes with zero goal squares; it has no stale-baseline test. The lead-the-eye arrow gate iterates FIRST_CLASS_OPENING_IDS only (pro/anti arrows ungated). proRepPlanAccuracy accepts a '<sq>-<piece>' claim if true at ANY frame of the line. groundingPlans iterates grounding-items.json, so mp-gleksystem-traditional-f4 (no cached item) was never graded. narrationFactCheck checks three moved-piece patterns; none of the errors in the findings above match them.
findings.fix: Make the wrong anchor impossible: per displayed tab assert criticalPositionFen == Watch terminus or a proven continuation, include gambits.json; build colorMap from pro.openings + anti + gambits and fail on zero goal squares; run lead-eye on all plans; check claims at the spoken frame; iterate plans, not cache items.

findings.evidence:
I ran Stockfish on each lesson's final position from the student's side. The first number is depth 16; the second, where present, is a depth-21 re-check.
- Samay 2…e6: 'freer game … Black stays cramped'. Engine: −1.12, then −1.26.
- Carlsen Scandinavian: 'comfortable … easy play'. Engine: −1.10, then −1.19.
- Aman Caro main/Advance: 'Comfortable equality'. Engine: −0.94, then −1.04.
- Hikaru vs Austrian: 'counterplay is fully in the game'. Engine: −1.13, then −1.03.

result.coverage:
What I checked: all 82 pro openings in src/data/pro-repertoires.json, across 8 players (naroditsky, gothamchess, ericrosen, samayraina, carlsen, caruana, hikaru, aman), and every registered pro lesson (367 lessons, 1,706 beats, from getAllLessonScripts).

Checks with clean results:
- Legality: chess.js replayed every main PGN, variation PGN, trapLine, warningLine and lesson beat. All are legal.
- Wiring: every pro opening has a lesson, with no orientation mismatch.
- Live keys: no orphan lesson keys. All 1,554 pro subline narration keys, plus the opening map, plan, model-game and common-mistake keys, point at live ids.

Checks that produced findings:
- Middlegame reach: the shared helper ran on every PGN and every deepest lesson beat.
- Play versus Watch/Learn/Practice: compared for every variation.
- Grounding: data/sources trees (only nodes with 5 or more games), deep spines, public/data/pro-game-references.json and model games.
- Soundness: Stockfish at depth 15-16 on all 367 lesson endings and all 57 trap/warning endings.
- Claim scans: automated pattern scans for pin, attack, doubled, isolated, bishop pair, long diagonal and open file over all beats and read-aloud JSON fields. Every case reported was then checked by hand on the replayed board.
- Text scans: names, pronouns, statistics and move numbers across lessons, pro-repertoires.json read-aloud fields and sublineNarration (subline text was scanned for these only).
- Orphan scans: classification keys, trap-lesson reachability, exports, test baselines and the mining scripts.

Limits:
- There was no full manual read of every beat. Claims phrased in ways the patterns miss may remain.
- Arrows were checked only through the existing geometry gate and its baseline.
- Plans, model games and common mistakes were checked for live keys only, not their narration.
- Grounding is limited to on-disk data. There is no raw chess.com corpus, trees drop paths under 5 games, and Gotham London and Samay King's Gambit have no tree (Samay Caro/French trees hold only 2-3 games on a different move order).
- Ten positions were re-checked at depth 20-21, above the task's depth cap of 18. Depth-16 numbers are given alongside them, and the conclusions hold at depth 16.

Process notes:
- The phase was read-only, so the orphaned code from old builds is reported with exact deletion lists, not deleted.
- No builds or tests were run.
- OpeningDetailPage.tsx has uncommitted edits from another session in /home/user/wt-work. Its line numbers above are from the current working tree; every other cited file is unmodified at HEAD d58defc8d.

I checked the data only, read-only, against HEAD ea7ddeaf0. That commit (F04 gem cut) landed during the audit and changed 2 lines of punish-gems.json and punishGems.ts; the findings hold for HEAD.

**Gems (all 389):** I replayed every gem in punish-gems.json (344) and gambit-punish-gems.json (45) with chess.js:
- playLine equals lineMoves + slip + punishSeq; legality and canonical SAN checked: all OK.

- Orientation against the opening's color (repertoire, pro and gambits files): 1 reversed gem.
- Also checked: tier against engineCp, gemId uniqueness, duplicate positions, mainMove.

**Narration (all 388 narrated gems):**
- The SAN that opens each watch/learn line against the move on that ply.
- The slip and punish beats name their moves.
- Side prefixes, material claims against the board, and scans for numbers (V8) and move numbers (V9).
- I called gemsForPosition() at the twin positions.

**Engine:** Stockfish 18 WASM through node, depth 18, single thread, multipv 3. The machine was shared (load 8–17).
- All 69 trap gems (61 distinct positions), all 54 from the plan doc plus the 15 gambit ones, and 17 near-bar or conflicting twins: eval after the opponent's best defence to the punish, and material along the engine line.
- 66 more positions: slip and end positions for the 19 masterclass named-trap lessons, all 19 repertoire.json lines, 5 gambits.json lines, 2 anti-openings.json lines, and 5 pro-rep spot checks against trap-engine-verification.json (they agree within about 15cp).
- 5 targeted checks: Tarrasch Nd4 and …Qd7, Pierce …Qxd5, Copycat, Mortimer.

**Trap lesson files:** all 17 *Trap* files (70 lessons: 19 named, 51 pro-Naroditsky).
- Beat legality and canonical SAN, beat narration against the beat's last move and side, and playable-line conversion.

**Repertoire trap/warning lines:** repertoire.json (7/12), pro-repertoires.json (49/8, using the repo's depth-22 manifest for all 57), gambits.json (2/3), anti-openings.json (2/0), both classification files, and the manifest.

findings.title: Other false board claims in the registered Vienna and Italian trap lessons
findings.where: src/data/lessons/viennaTrapLessons.ts:427, 450, 457-458, 471 (copycat-qg4); 586-629 (steinitz-gambit); 182, 203, 210-211 (hamppe-allgaier); 287 (hamppe-muzio); 119 (wurzburger); src/data/lessons/italianGameTrapLessons.ts:59
findings.evidence:
Checked with chess.js on each beat's board.
- copycat-qg4:
  - 'Qxf2+ would be checkmate ... no escape squares': after ...Qxf2+, Kd1 is legal.
  - 'Kd1!! a brilliant in-between move': Kd1 is the only legal move.
  - 'the Black queen is trapped': it has 9 moves, including Qxd5, Qxc4 and Qxb2.
  - 'Kf8 ... removing the rook target': the king moved, not the rook.
  - 'Nd5 supported by the Qf3 and the c2/e4 pawn duo': the e4 pawn blocks Qf3 from d5, and c2 does not cover d5.
- steinitz-gambit:
  - 'the pin is illusory': the f3-knight has no legal move (absolute pin to Ke2).
  - 'Bg4 also defends the queen': it does not defend h4.
  - 'the e1-h4 diagonal is blocked by the e4 pawn': e4 is not on that diagonal.
  - 'threatens Bxd6 winning ANOTHER pawn': c7 recaptures.
  - 'Nf3 covers the e1-h4 diagonal': f3 is not on it.
- hamppe-allgaier:
  - 'open h-file': there are pawns on h4 and h6.
  - 'Nb8 ... still on its starting square': the knight is on c6.
  - 'Bd5 aims at b7': the c6-knight blocks it.
  - 'the Bb3-pivot in the Wurzburger setup': the Wurzburger lesson never plays Bb3.
- hamppe-muzio: 'e5 opens the h2-b8 diagonal ... Bxh6 ideas': the pawn now stands on that diagonal, and h6 is empty.
- wurzburger: 'White still has the bishop pair': both sides have both bishops.
- fried-liver: 'Qf3+ ... she skewers the loose d5-knight': the queen hits f7 and d5 on different lines, which is a fork.
These lessons are in the masterclass registry (registry.ts:26 and :32), yet narrationAccuracy does not check these claim types.
findings.fix: Rewrite the beats to match their boards. Add pin, fork-vs-skewer, mate and only-move checks to the lesson accuracy gate.

findings.title: Trap and warning line explanations contradict their own PGNs, and several PGNs contain unrelated one-move blunders
findings.where: src/data/repertoire.json:1494, 1499, 1504, 2284, 862, 2617, 1099, 3108; src/data/gambits.json:274-288; src/data/pro-repertoires.json:4406, 4576, 5510. Explanations are shown on warning tiles (OpeningDetailPage.tsx:2426-2427), and trap names are spoken in the coach's opening-traps answer (coachApi.ts:4403-4405)
findings.evidence:
Each PGN was replayed with chess.js and engine-checked at depth 18 at its end.
- petrov 'Nxf7 Refutation': there is no Nxf7 in the PGN. The text says 'instead of the main 3.Nxe5', but the PGN plays 3.Nxe5. 'The queen invades to e1 with check' is not in the line.
- petrov 'Wrong Move Order Punishment' (a trapLine, i.e. a student weapon): it starts with the student's own 3...Nxe4?. The text promises a queen trade and a 'drawable' endgame; the PGN has no queen trade and ends ...Qxa1+.
- petrov 'Steinitz d4 Counter': there is no slip in it.
  - 'opens the b-file for Black': bxc3 half-opens the b-file for White.
  - 'with the bishop pair': both sides keep both bishops.
  - It ends with White hanging a rook: Re1?? Rxe1+, engine +743.
- grunfeld 'Premature Center Grab': the text describes '...Bxa1? ... trap the bishop in the corner'. The PGN instead plays ...Bxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4 Bxf7+ Kxf7 Qxd4.
- sveshnikov 'Premature d5 Push': the text says 'a shattered center'. The PGN ends 8...Qxd5?? 9.Qxd5, losing the queen (-588).
- budapest 'Fajarowicz Overreach': the text says 'White consolidates the extra pawn'. The PGN ends ...Qxe5?? Nxe5 Nxe5 (-554); at a3 the engine has only -94.
- caro 'Advance Bishop Exchange Danger': the f6-knight stands en prise to e5xf6 for three White moves and is never taken; end -325, best exf6.
- stafford 'Aggressive e5 Refutation': the text describes 5.e5, but the PGN stops at 4...dxc6. Two other stafford warnings have the identical PGN.
- Mislabels in pro-repertoires.json:
  - pro-carlsen-sicilian '...Nxe4 drops the queen': the line loses a knight for a pawn (-277).
  - pro-carlsen-nimzo 'loses material to Nxe4': the PGN plays Qxe4.
  - pro-carlsen-closed-sicilian 'nothing recaptures on d5': e4xd5 does.
- evans 'Declining Into Passivity' (a White warningLine): the text praises White's 'dominant center', but the line ends -171 for White.
findings.fix: Rebuild these lines from the database and engine, or delete them. Derive each explanation from its own PGN. Never ship a warning whose PGN contains an unrelated one-move blunder.
